newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg CEO's $2.7 million compensation down from 1995.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg CEO's $2.7 million compensation down from 1995.

text.p: Kellogg Co. said Thursday that Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Arnold Langbo took home $2.7 million from compensation and stock options in 1996, down 33 percent from 1995.

Langbo earned a higher base salary in 1996 -- $932,500 compared with $880,000 -- but his bonus fell by more than half to $315,000 from $765,000 because the world's largest cereal maker fell short of its earnings per share target for 1996.
Langbo exercised stock options worth $1,460,070 in 1996, versus $2,392,805 from options a year before. Also in 1996, the company granted him 160,000 new stock options that it valued at $2,094,400.
The figures were included in Kellogg's 1996 proxy statement filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Kellogg said it used the Black-Scholes model to calculate the future value of the 160,000 new options Langbo was granted. However, the options, which expire March 15, 2006, carry an exercise price of $77.50 each -- higher than the $66.75 a share the stock ended at Thursday.
A year ago, Langbo was granted 150,000 new options then valued at $1,749,000.

The company said bonuses for all employees fell by half because Kellogg hit 80 percent of its 1996 earnings per share goal. Kellogg earned $531 million, or $2.50 a share, on revenues of $6.68 billion in 1996, including several one-time items.
In 1995, Kellogg earned $490.3 million, or $2.24 a share, on revenues of $7.0 billion.
Kellogg said it scheduled its annual shareholders meeting for 1 p.m. EDT April 25 at the W.K. Kellogg Auditorium in Battle Creek, Mich.
